title: Designing a GPU-Accelerated Communication Layer for Efficient Fluid-Structure Interaction Computations on Heterogeneous Systems
problem: Fluid-structure interaction codes designed for CPU-based distributed systems with flexible design must be redesigned for efficient execution on GPU-accelerated heterogeneous systems. This requires offloading communication tasks to GPUs while maintaining correctness and managing GPU memory constraints.
motivation: Biological simulations with increasingly larger cell counts demand deployment on heterogeneous supercomputing resources to achieve practical time-to-solution for large-scale scientific discovery.
method: The authors move the task of sending data between system components from CPUs to GPUs, since GPUs can do this work much faster. They reorganize how data is stored so GPUs can access it without wasting time. They also develop new algorithms that speed up the overall computation. They validate the approach on Polaris and Frontier supercomputers using real simulations involving millions of deformable cells.
key_novelty: The key idea is moving communication work from CPUs to GPUs and redesigning data structures so GPUs can access them efficiently.
contributions: GPU-accelerated communication layer design for fluid-structure interaction on heterogeneous systems
Analysis of trade-offs between offloading communication to GPU versus code efficiency and memory footprint
New algorithms that significantly reduce time-to-solution for FSI computations
Design guidance for HPC applications implementing communication layers on heterogeneous architectures
